title: Balanced flows do not choose a stock
hook: The same arrival and loss rates can leave different stocks unchanged.

doesNotKnow: Explain why fixed balanced flows cannot locate a unique equilibrium.

misconception: Balanced rates identify one particular equilibrium stock.
objective: Explain why fixed balanced flows cannot locate a unique equilibrium.

claims.text: Island species numbers reflect both immigration and extinction.
Robert H. MacArthur and Edward O. Wilson, The Theory of Island Biogeography (1967)
Balanced flows retain {A} and {B}. Equal arrivals and losses stop net change at either stock; fixed flows do not select a unique equilibrium.
Does it hold up? Counts and rates are stipulated. Species-dependent curves and empirical island predictions are not modeled.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: Reservoirs start at 5 and 12. Each gains and loses 2 per step. Do they converge?
recall.why: Both net flows are zero, so each starting stock is retained.
